newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Serono files suit against Schering unit.
newsitem.headline: Serono files suit against Schering unit.

text.p: Pharmaceuticals group Ares-Serono said its U.S. subsidiary Serono Laboratories, based in Norwell, Mass., had filed suit against Berlex Laboratories, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Germany's Schering AG, to invalidate Berlex's recombinant interferon beta patent.
Serono said in a statement that it filed the complaint in the U.S. District Court for Massachusetts against Berlex.
The complaint seeks a declatory judgement of non-infringement and invalidity of U.S. Patent number 5,376,567 entitled "Expression of interferon genes in Chinese hamster ovary cells."
The patent is also known as the McCormick patent.

The complaint contends that Serono's recombinant human interferon beta 1-a product Rebif, its manufacturing process and the intermediates used in Rebif's manufacture do not infringe on the McCormick patent and the patent is invalid.
A similar action filed by Biogen Inc. with respect to the McCormick patent is already pending in the same court with respect to Biogen's recombinant interferon beta-1a.

"The filing of this litigation reflects Ares-Serono's clear intent to enter the United States market as soon as possible with its recombinant interferon beta-1a Rebif," the statement quoted Ares-Serono's chief executive Ernesto Bertarelli as saying.
Ares-Serono has already obtained orphan drug status from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the treatment of secondary progressive multiple sclerosis.
